assumption_visibility.rationale: Assumptions are explicitly documented: Chrome browser availability, Docker/Docker Compose installation, 2D physics simulation sufficiency, WebSocket/HTTP polling for real-time communication, and TypeScript/Node.js performance adequacy. These cover technical infrastructure and architectural decisions.

evidence_grounding.rationale: Evidence refs are present and grounded in available context: task metadata containing user requirements, explicit task constraints (localRunRequired, humanAcceptanceAfterLocalStart, deploymentExcluded), project context (XS complexity, web-app type), and repository state (no existing artifacts).

problem_clarity.rationale: Problem statement clearly defines a physics-based docking simulation inspired by Elite, with specific requirements for realistic physics (inertia, thrust, rotation), successful docking vs hull impact failure modes, and scope boundaries (proof-of-concept focusing on essential docking mechanics, not a full game).

risk_visibility.rationale: Risks are explicitly documented with clear categories: technical risks (physics realism, real-time performance, 3D vs 2D expectations, automated test nondeterminism) and adoption risk (user expectation mismatch). These are manageable through proper engineering practices.

scope_boundedness.rationale: Candidate scope is well-defined with clear MVP boundaries: web-based simulation with spacecraft and rotating station, physics-based movement controls, keyboard input handling, Chrome visualization, collision detection for both docking success and failure, at least one automated test, and single-command startup via docker compose up.

stakeholder_coverage.rationale: Stakeholders are identified: primary user (developer requesting the simulation), factory system (requiring verifiable automated tests), and future users who may extend the simulation. This covers immediate needs and downstream consumers.

unknowns_manageability.rationale: Unknowns are identified and bounded: physics engine choice (existing vs custom), visualization approach (Canvas/WebGL/libraries), automated test strategy, performance requirements, and station rotation complexity impact. All are resolvable during implementation and do not prevent discovery settlement.

non_blocking_gaps.description: Performance requirements (frame rate, latency) not specified; may affect physics realism perception but can be tuned during implementation.
3D vs 2D visualization expectation not explicitly confirmed; assumption of 2D sufficiency may need validation during implementation.

rationale: The Proposal demonstrates strong readiness across all seven dimensions. Problem statement is clear and focused, scope is well-bounded with explicit MVP criteria, stakeholders are identified, assumptions and unknowns are documented, risks are visible and manageable, and evidence is grounded in available context. The two non-blocking gaps (performance requirements, 3D vs 2D expectation) are implementation concerns that can be addressed during development without blocking discovery settlement. The recommended outcome of 'go' in the rationale aligns with the overall readiness verdict.
